# Separate distributed device discovery, synchronization and data retrieval

## Platform difference

Discovering an OH device and requesting synchronization do not establish that application data was retrieved or applied.

## Implementation

Etohos adds device discovery and device_list channel handling. Its snapshot publishes shared_config through a device-collaboration KV store and requests PUSH_PULL synchronization, but the explicit requestConfigFromDevice path leaves the get operation commented and returns null from an empty value. A remote-change callback is a separate delivery route.

## Applicability

This is a partly implemented native collaboration feature, dependent on device/account/trust/permission conditions not validated by the study.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

The KV settings include encrypt:false and autoSync:true and the inspected code logs sensitive-looking configuration data. These are source configuration facts, not a statement about OS transport encryption or proof of exploitability. Review sharing scope and log content before adopting the pattern.

## Verification

Test discovery separately from pairing/trust, publish, synchronization completion, explicit pull, remote-change delivery and application of the retrieved configuration; test denied permissions and empty results.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
